hints: Find the total displacement reached before the particle returns to its starting point by adding the initial 50 m to the distance covered in the next 10 s.
Calculate the displacement at $t = 20\text{ s}$ using distance = speed $\times$ time for the second stage.
Use the definition of velocity as the gradient of the displacement-time graph, dividing the change in displacement by the time interval of 20 s.
walkthrough:
Calculate the total displacement reached before the particle begins returning to the origin:
$$s = 50 + 2 \times 10 = 50 + 20 = 70\text{ m}$$

Find the velocity during the final 20 s ($t = 40\text{ s}$ to $t = 60\text{ s}$) from the gradient of the displacement-time graph:
$$v = \frac{\Delta s}{\Delta t} = \frac{0 - 70}{60 - 40} = -\frac{70}{20} = -3.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
teacher_walkthrough: First, determine the maximum displacement reached by the particle before it begins its return journey. In the first 10 s, it travels 50 m. For the next 10 s, it travels at a constant velocity of $2\text{ m s}^{-1}$:

Calculate the displacement covered during this second stage:
$$s_2 = v_2 \times t_2 = 2 \times 10 = 20\text{ m}$$

Add this to the initial 50 m to find the total displacement at $t = 20\text{ s}$:
$$s_{\text{total}} = 50 + 20 = 70\text{ m}$$

The particle remains at rest from $t = 20\text{ s}$ to $t = 40\text{ s}$, so its displacement remains $70\text{ m}$ at $t = 40\text{ s}$. It then returns to its starting point ($s = 0$) at $t = 60\text{ s}$.

Recall that velocity on a displacement-time graph is represented by the gradient of the line segment:
$$v = \frac{s_2 - s_1}{t_2 - t_1}$$

Substitute the coordinates $(t_1, s_1) = (40, 70)$ and $(t_2, s_2) = (60, 0)$ into the gradient formula:
$$v = \frac{0 - 70}{60 - 40} = \frac{-70}{20} = -3.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
The negative sign confirms that the particle is moving in the reverse direction back towards the origin.

ai_rubric.Interpreting Motion Graphs: Shows $50 + 2 \times 10 = 70\text{ m}$ and calculates $-70 / 20 = -3.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

hints: Since each section of the displacement-time graph is a straight line, each section has a constant gradient, meaning the velocity is constant on each interval.
Calculate the constant velocity for each interval: 0 to 10 s, 10 to 20 s, 20 to 40 s, and 40 to 60 s.
Draw a stepped velocity-time graph consisting of four horizontal line segments with clearly labelled axes and values.
walkthrough:
Determine the constant velocity for each of the four stages from the gradients:
$$\text{For } 0 \le t < 10:\quad v = \frac{50}{10} = 5\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
$$\text{For } 10 < t < 20:\quad v = 2\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
$$\text{For } 20 < t < 40:\quad v = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
$$\text{For } 40 < t \le 60:\quad v = -3.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

The resulting velocity-time graph is a stepped diagram consisting of four horizontal line segments with key values $5$, $2$, $0$, and $-3.5$ on the $v$-axis at times $10$, $20$, $40$, and $60$ on the $t$-axis.
teacher_walkthrough: Because the displacement-time graph is made of straight line segments, the particle moves at constant velocity during each distinct time interval. On a velocity-time graph, constant velocities are represented by horizontal line segments.

Calculate the velocity for the first interval $0 \le t \le 10\text{ s}$ using the gradient:
$$v_1 = \frac{\Delta s}{\Delta t} = \frac{50 - 0}{10 - 0} = 5\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

For the second interval $10 \le t \le 20\text{ s}$, the question directly states that the speed is constant:
$$v_2 = 2\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

For the third interval $20 \le t \le 40\text{ s}$, the particle is at rest for 20 s:
$$v_3 = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

For the fourth interval $40 \le t \le 60\text{ s}$, use the velocity found in part (a):
$$v_4 = -3.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

To draw the velocity-time sketch: draw a horizontal line segment at $v = 5$ from $t = 0$ to $t = 10$; a horizontal line segment at $v = 2$ from $t = 10$ to $t = 20$; a horizontal line segment along the time axis ($v = 0$) from $t = 20$ to $t = 40$; and a horizontal line segment below the axis at $v = -3.5$ from $t = 40$ to $t = 60$. Label the values $5$, $2$, $0$, and $-3.5$ on the $v$-axis and $10$, $20$, $40$, and $60$ on the $t$-axis.
